designs.title: Humpback Whale
designs.why: Dynamic breaching pose and dense engraving sell it, but it is the most-copied tee on Etsy and too close to the founder's own whale reference to feel new.

designs.title: Ammonite
designs.why: Best buy in the run: fills the chest, reads from across a room, photographs crisply, and feels like a real museum-store object rather than an AI stock image.

designs.title: Gaff Cutter
designs.why: Scratchy, light line work goes faint on the tee and looks like a weak copy of the sailboat reference; it needs a clean technical elevation with a hull section and rigging callouts.

designs.title: Hot Air Balloon
designs.why: Charming subject with a clean silhouette, but it prints small and pale, with too much empty envelope; scale it up and add rigging or construction detail to justify $50.

designs.title: Scooter
designs.why: Reads as a Vespa (trademark risk), and its soft airbrush shading will turn to mushy halftone grey; it looks like generic AI clip art, not an engraving.

designs.title: Colonial House
designs.why: Closest to the founder's taste: dense pen-and-ink detail with palms, strong in the hand, and a photo that stands out on the white tee.

designs.title: Lighthouse
designs.why: Competent but generic gift-shop lighthouse, thin and small on the back; it needs a cutaway or elevation with dimensions, or a specific named lighthouse, to stand out.

designs.title: Luna Moth
designs.why: The wing shapes and eyespots are off for a real Actias luna and the body looks AI-made; it is pale on the tee and competes with thousands of 'witchy moth' shirts.

designs.title: Sunflower
designs.why: Stock-image botanical with no point of view; the most generic AI 'vintage engraving' look in the run and nothing a curated shop would pick out.

designs.title: Compass
designs.why: Open-lid view stacks two circles into an odd figure-eight on the body, and the dial is nearly empty; show it face-on with a dense rose and bezel markings.

designs.title: Rangefinder Camera
designs.why: Desirable object with crisp detail and good tonal range, but the wide landscape format prints as a small band, and the Leica-like body needs its branding kept off.

designs.title: Red Deer
designs.why: Well rendered but it is the stock AI stag; the hooves fade into nothing, and it would need a study-sheet treatment (antler details, skull) to differ from the forest-tee crowd.

designs.title: Grey Heron
designs.why: Elegant silhouette, but the legs and base dissolve into faint hatching that will vanish at 30 lpi, and the bird floats small and top-heavy on the back.

suggestions: Lean into multi-view study sheets (subject plus 3-5 numbered detail views, as in the whale reference); that layout is the clearest way to stand apart from single-subject AI engraving tees.

Pick specific, named, nerd-pleasing subjects (a particular locomotive, telescope or diving helmet, an Ernst Haeckel-style radiolarian) over generic categories like 'sunflower', 'deer' or 'lighthouse'.
Fill the print area: at least 10-11 inches wide with dense black mass. Thin pale line art and landscape-format art both read as tiny and washed out in photos.
Ban soft airbrush or gradient shading in the source art; ask for hard hatching and stipple only, so the 30 lpi halftone does not turn the midtones into grey mush.

Avoid repeating the founder's references and branded shapes (Vespa, Leica): one sailboat and one whale are enough, so spend the next slots on unexplored types such as maps, anatomy, tools or architecture sections.
overall: Only Ammonite and Colonial House feel like $50 museum-store tees; Whale and Camera are sellable, most of the rest is competent but generic AI engraving that prints too small and pale on white, and Sunflower should go.
